challenge.better_approach: Considered one shared planted-breach helper, but RULE 1 keeps each component's fixture in its own proofs, so each file carries its own tooth. Considered dropping the not-blind half altogether; a sieve returning [] would then pass every tooth.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That the sieve resolves source and target from charters on disk alone, so a scratch tree with empty charters reproduces a real breach. Measured 2026-11-16: the built tooth returns the planted row with both resolved.
challenge.prior_art: cairn/tools/bus_client/proofs/test_bus_client_proofs_measure_only_bus_client.py:49-62 (ticket 7806309a8018) and the harbor tooth in cairn/tools/bus_client/proofs/test_the_harbor_source_asks_over_the_bus.py (ticket bfa522282b17) already do exactly this; this copies them.
challenge.real_collision: None: the live tooth's claim (no breach from this component) is unchanged; only its not-blind half moves to a fixture.

answers.falsifier: The planted tooth names exactly the planted row, and the live tooth passes with 0 breaches elsewhere. Red on origin/main, measured: '0 breach(es) in all'. Horizon: the proof's next reseal.
answers.how: In each of cairn/tools/system_word/proofs/test_system_word_proofs_measure_only_system_word.py: add test_the_sieve_names_a_planted_breach, which builds a scratch tree with charters at the component and its target and one planted.py importing the target, asks encapsulation_breaches over it through inspect_wire, and checks the sieve returns exactly that row (file, line 1, source, target). It runs first in the proof's teeth. The live tooth drops 'and bool(breaches)' and keeps 'not mine'. This is the pattern in cairn/tools/bus_client/proofs/test_bus_client_proofs_measure_only_bus_client.py:49-62.
answers.traces_to: Law 8 and Law 9: a proof whose green needs the world to stay dirty is one a correct world fails, so it measures the world, not the component.
answers.what: system word's measure-only proof shows the encapsulation sieve can see by planting one breach in a scratch tree, not by needing a breach somewhere in the live repo.

bullets.text: system word's not-blind guard turned red because the repo came clean, not because the sieve went blind.
